newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks climb to 8th straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks climb to 8th straight record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks chalked up their eighth successive record close on Wednesday after recovering from early profit-taking as dealers jumped in to snap up bargains on strong trade numbers, dealers said.
"We had intraday profit-taking and foreign buying today, but the sheer flow of funds we have seen is blowing away all market parameters," said Gerardo Copca, an analyst at the Finamex brokerage.
"Revised trade figures turned it around," he added.
Final closing prices showed the blue-chip IPC index was up 26.47 points, or 0.55 percent, at 4,862.96.
The Finance Ministry revised May's trade surplus up to $220 million, from a preliminary $88 million, in late morning dealing.
"Buyers stepped in after the data, and the market still feels strong. Dealing picked up in the last two hours," a floor trader said.
"Besides, you now have dealers that don't want to let go of paper and offer high prices who are tussling with buyers and that keeps prices up," he added.
Trading volume recovered from a slow start to a brisk 121.9 million shares.

Dealers said market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico once again hauled up the market, and gained 35 centavos (4 cents) to a peso record of 21.25 ($2.70). The telecommunications company's American Depository Receipts ended up 13/16 to 54-1/8, a level unseen since the December 1994 peso crash.

Traders also drew attention to market newcomer Wings. The restaurant chain gained 24 centavos (3 cents) to 3.18 pesos (40 cents) amid heavy demand from foreign buyers driven by the company's expansion plans, they said.
On the broad market, gainers outstripped sliders by 67 to 33 out of a total of 119 stocks that changed hands.
